ana-the-room.caption: A single THE Room suite (seat 12H) seen from the aisle: the tall sliding door panel swung open, the wide seat with its fabric-lined shell, the 24-inch monitor and the ottoman/footrest opposite
The 777-300ER business class cabin looking down the aisle - rows of THE Room suites in alternating forward- and rear-facing pairs, each with its own screen and full-height partition
Two adjacent THE Room suites with the seats laid fully flat into beds, the headrest cushions and a blue pillow in place and the divider between the pair raised
The suite's large bi-fold dining table extended over the seat, with the seat control panel alongside

arashiyama.caption: The Sagano bamboo path: the paved walkway running between woven-bamboo fences with dense green culms towering on both sides and closing overhead, a handful of walkers small in the middle distance
Togetsukyo bridge stretched low across the Katsura river with the Arashiyama mountainside behind it in full autumn colour, mist lifting off the ridge and the wide gravel riverbank in the foreground

Tenryu-ji's Sogen-chi pond garden in autumn: standing rock arrangements set into the green water, the mown bank in front, and the whole Arashiyama hillside behind turned scarlet and orange as borrowed scenery

On board a Hozugawa-kudari boat: a boatman in happi coat standing at the gunwale working a long pole through white water in the gorge, a second crewman beside him, autumn foliage on the rock walls either side. The bench sign gives the boat's capacity as 30. Photographed 26 November

aso-caldera.caption: Looking down into Nakadake's active first crater from the rim path: the pale turquoise acid crater lake at the bottom, banded red-and-ochre crater walls, and steam pouring off the water
Horses grazing loose on the flat grass of Kusasenri, with the old crater wall behind them covered in flowering miyama-kirishima azalea
The road up onto the volcano curving away between grass banks and log guardrails, with the grey ash-covered flank of Nakadake filling the skyline ahead
A dense ash-and-steam plume rising from Nakadake's crater against a blue sky, seen across a hillside of autumn susuki pampas grass from the viewpoint railing near Kusasenri

beniya-mukayu.caption: The arrival approach: a stone-slab path over gravel running under a canopy of maples to the low, dark entrance, with a paper andon lantern lit at the side.
The tiled roof and plaster wall of the garden tea house showing through the maples above the moss floor of the forest garden.
Roji stepping stones set into deep moss between ferns and shrubs in the forest garden.
The moss garden in full sun — a narrow stone-slab path running between leaning maples and a large pine, with a stone lantern and moss-covered boulders.
A guest room's split-bamboo veranda: two rattan lounge chairs and a glazed ceramic drum table facing a full-width opening onto the maple forest, behind a timber balustrade.
Interior of a Byakuroku suite — tatami room on the right opening through a reed screen onto the sunlit bamboo veranda, black-lacquered floor and a bed visible through the doorway at left.
A Western-style bedroom in the modern wing: low bed against a board-formed exposed-concrete wall, pale oak headboard shelf with gooseneck lamps, and a full-height glass wall onto a pine.
The Wakamurasaki room in winter — bamboo-floored veranda with two rattan chairs and floor cushions around a ceramic table, dark plank floor and straw-flecked plaster walls, bare trees outside.
The private open-air onsen bath of a Byakuroku Terrace Suite: a round hinoki tub set into a cedar deck under a timber ceiling, with a slatted screen opening onto the forest garden.
The communal bath "Usuko" — a sunken dark-stone tub in a room lined entirely in hinoki, with a low horizontal window and lantern-lit bamboo screen framing the bamboo grove outside.
Horin, the restaurant: a grid of slender black columns over dark plank floors, black tables with Wishbone chairs, and a glazed wall onto the terrace and the property's old pine.
A lidded black lacquer soup bowl and chopsticks on a lacquer tray at a table in the restaurant, with the timber deck and garden beyond the open frame.
Female snow crab (kobako-gani) — two crabs dressed back into their shells with layered leg meat and orange roe, set on cedar sprigs on a blue-and-white porcelain plate.
A chilled soup served inside a hollowed-out cucumber, on a celadon square plate with a black lacquer spoon and a sprig of green maple.
The library: black open shelving holding books, framed prints and objects around a driftwood branch, beside a long dark table and a window onto the maples.

Morning yoga in the glass-walled hall — a guest in a lunge silhouetted against the deck, the old pine and a bank of red autumn maples. Shot dated 25 November, so this is the late-November look of the garden.

byodo-in-uji.caption: The Phoenix Hall in low sun, its vermilion corridors and central hall mirrored whole in the still water of the Aji-ike pond - the composition used on the 10-yen coin
The Phoenix Hall from across the pond at peak autumn, with the arched vermilion bridge in the foreground and maples in full scarlet along the far bank
One of the pair of gilt-bronze phoenixes standing on the ridge-end of the Phoenix Hall roof, wings spread, against the wooded hillside behind
The central hall and the south corridor's corner tower framed by red maples overhead and yellow ginkgo below, in autumn

cenci-kyoto.caption: The street front at night: a long illuminated slot window cut into the plastered wall revealing the brick barrel vault inside with the script 'cenci' sign, next to the lit entrance door with its wrought-iron grille

The dining room: a vaulted plaster ceiling springing from a tree-like timber column, walnut tables laid with slate chargers and starburst-cut glass tumblers, a chandelier and wall sconces, and a glazed wall onto the rock-and-fern courtyard
Risotto with shredded green cabbage and herbs, topped with slices of smoked pork loin and a spoonful of chopped mushroom-and-nut relish, in a matte black bowl
Main course: a slice of rare red meat with charred savoy cabbage, a red-wine reduction, and a small croquette topped with crisp fried lotus root on a puree, on a plain white plate
Dessert: a quenelle of matcha ice cream over cream and sliced strawberries on a pale disc, with matcha powder and a golden crumble, in a hand-formed ragged-rim ceramic bowl
Four cooks in white jackets and navy aprons working side by side at the marble pass under brass heat lamps in the open kitchen

eikando.caption: Hojo-ike pond at peak autumn: banks of scarlet and orange maples on every side, the low arched stone bridge crossing the water, and the whole scene doubled in the still surface under a clear blue sky. Photographed in November
The night illumination: the two-storey Tahoto pagoda floodlit blue-white on its hillside, floating above a mass of uplit maples burning orange and crimson against the black hillside
The Tahoto pagoda seen by day from below, its dark roof breaking the treeline on the wooded slope above a wall of red and orange maples, with the pond in the foreground
Inside one of Eikando's covered wooden corridors that link the halls up the hillside: worn plank floor, exposed rafters and bracketing, and rows of five-colour Buddhist banners hung along both sides

ezo-momonga.caption: An Ezo momonga filling the mouth of its nest hole, front paws on the rim — the pale grey-buff winter coat, white cheeks and chin, enormous black eyes and short rounded ears that identify Pteromys volans orii
A whole animal in the open: an Ezo momonga sitting upright on a broken branch stub against the trunk, paws tucked together, facing the camera — roughly hand-sized, about 15 cm of body
An Ezo momonga mid-glide against a clear blue twilight sky, patagium stretched square between wrists and ankles and the flattened tail trailing behind
An Ezo momonga in profile part-way along a lichen-covered branch in blue dusk light, the fringe of skin along its flank visible — this is the light level the animals actually emerge in
Two Ezo momonga on the same trunk at dusk, one head-down above the other, both looking straight down at the camera
What the watch actually looks like: the guide and a client standing quietly in bare birch and oak woodland with patchy snow on the ground, a long lens on a tripod trained on a nest tree

fukuoka-yatai.caption: Six customers packed shoulder to shoulder along a yatai counter at night, clinking beer glasses across the wood with the cook leaning in, under a hanging wave-pattern noren and bare bulb light

A single yatai set up for the evening, flanked by two big glowing white paper lanterns, its indigo noren printed with a red Hakata Niwaka festival mask, folding stools ready behind clear plastic weather sheeting and yellow ginkgo leaves on the pavement
A yatai in Nakasu at night, every stool taken and a second row of people standing behind, steam off the griddle, the stall's red illuminated sign and blue-lit buildings overhead

The front of a yatai after dark, its awning hung with a row of magenta and yellow cloth banners advertising oden, udon, tsukune, tempura and grilled offal, steam rising off a pot on the counter and empty stools along the front

gekkoju.caption: The main gate: a heavy thatched roof over dark timber, twin studded wooden doors, a hanging iron lantern and a small name plaque reading 月洸樹, reached by a gravel path through the woods

The ryokan seen from above at sunset: dark standing-seam metal roofs stepping down the hillside, the vermilion covered bridge linking the buildings, and ridge after ridge of forested Kyushu mountains behind
The grounds at blue hour: a stone-lined hot-spring stream and shallow foot-bath pools crossed by a dark timber deck, lit by low cube lanterns, with the black-timber main lodge glowing behind

Low sun breaking through the trees over the bathing terrace, with loungers on the deck, a rock-edged pool in the foreground and the wooded Kurokawa valley falling away beyond; the maples are just beginning to turn

A villa's double-height living room: exposed blackened roof trusses over ochre plaster walls, oak floors, deep sofas and armchairs facing a wall-set TV in rough stone, a mezzanine gallery above, a raised tatami platform with a tea counter at the back, and glass doors onto a deck in the trees

A villa sitting room at night: chequerboard tatami, a faceted dark-wood low table with patchwork floor cushions, a long bench and TV set into a rough stone wall, and two glazed openings onto a lantern-lit garden

A villa's tatami room under a coffered washi ceiling and a single paper lantern, with two round low tables, yellow and pink floor cushions, and a full-height glass wall onto a private deck and the forest

A villa's private indoor hot-spring bath: a large square sunken tub of dark stone under a soaring blackened timber roof, veined stone wall panels and a slatted clerestory, with sliding doors thrown open onto the deck and green hillside
The private open-air bath of the villa Tenshin (天心): a rectangular stone-edged tub on a timber deck, steam rising, ringed by maples in full autumn colour with the wooded valley beyond
The private open-air bath of the villa Kagetsu (佳月): a steaming timber tub set into the deck under a dark eave, water pouring from a bamboo spout, open on one side to the trees and hills

An open-air bath on the edge of the hillside in winter: still hot water in a stone-coped pool with a single candle lantern on the rim, looking straight out over snow-laden cedars to the snow-covered ridges opposite

The glass-walled lounge and dining pavilion at night, seen from the garden: a lit bar counter lined with stemware, timber posts and pendant lamps inside, seating groups beyond, and a crescent moon over the dark valley

A place laid for breakfast at one of the long dining tables, which has a sand-filled charcoal pit running down its centre with a wire grill over it; a compartmented lacquer box of small dishes, a paper-pot hot pot on its burner, grilled fish, rice and miso soup are set out around it

The dinner laid out from above on the charcoal-pit table: sashimi including horse and white fish, a nine-compartment appetiser tray, a lidded simmered dish, seasoned rice, a whole grilled spiny lobster in a black lacquer bowl, and dipping sauces
A staff member turning slices of marbled Kyushu beef with tongs on the charcoal grill set into the dining table, smoke rising, with sashimi, small dishes and bottles of local beer and sake around it

A kaiseki course set out on a tatami mat: abalone with peas, horse sashimi in a stone dish, a bamboo-shoot and cured-roe plate, a lidded white ceramic simmered dish, and an assortment of small seasonal bites on a white slab

gion.caption: Yasaka-dori in the early morning, the cobbled lane running downhill between wooden machiya with their street lanterns still lit, and the five-storey Yasaka Pagoda of Hokan-ji rising dead centre at the end of the street

A stone-paved Gion street after dark: two-storey wooden ochaya with bamboo inuyarai fences, noren curtains and lattice screens, warm light spilling from upstairs windows, a red cylindrical post box in the foreground and two figures walking away down the empty street

The Shirakawa canal in Gion, its shallow stone-walled channel running right up against the backs of the machiya, with sudare reed blinds, bamboo fencing and overhanging willow and cherry. Trees are in full green leaf, so this is a warm-season photograph

Gion at dusk in the rain: rows of red-and-white paper lanterns and the district's round red Gion lanterns hung along the machiya frontages, a Kyoto-cuisine restaurant's calligraphed signboard above, umbrellas moving down the street below

goh-fukuoka.caption: The dining room: a single long polished-wood communal table set for fourteen with white napkins and blue-and-white plates, lit by candles, city lights visible through the window along the left wall.

The restaurant's signature dish, captioned on its own site as abalone and shiitake mushrooms in browned butter sauce with aosa seaweed risotto: a whole abalone on a matte grey plate over herbed risotto, a pale brown sauce spooned across it.
A rare-cooked slice of red meat with a dark seared crust and cracked peppercorns, served with braised endive, an orange puree quenelle and a glossy brown sauce on a blue-and-white scalloped plate.
A red-lacquer bowl holding a lightly fried rectangular block in clear broth, topped with a sprig of flowering nanohana and a young sansho leaf.
Portrait of chef Takeshi 'Goh' Fukuyama in a black chef's shirt, seated at a dark wooden table with his hands clasped, labelled 'CHEF - Goh Fukuyama' on the restaurant's own page.

gora-byakudan.caption: The entrance at night: a white noren curtain brush-lettered 箱根強羅 白檀 (Hakone Gora Byakudan) hanging beside a fine bamboo screen, a small floor lantern lighting the flagstone approach and its mossy stone kerb
A low flat-roofed pavilion in the grounds lit from below at night, its open sides glowing white against the surrounding trees and a dark gravel forecourt

The lounge at first light: the full-height curved window wall looking out over a valley filled with low cloud and the ridgelines of the Hakone mountains, strings of faceted paper lanterns and low seating in the foreground
A timber deck with a woven lounger and cafe chairs behind a frameless glass balustrade, looking out over the treetops to the wooded Hakone hills and the town below

A guest room's tatami sitting area: a pale wood low table with floor chairs, a round woven armchair, a wall-length console with a television, and sliding glass onto a private terrace with chairs and greenery beyond

A tatami guest room seen down its length: a round paper pendant lamp over a long low table with round rattan floor chairs, shoji screens on both sides, a television in a recessed console, and the room opening at the far end onto the private open-air bath and trees

The sleeping area of a Japanese-Western guest room: twin low beds with white linen against a pale timber wall, a framed calligraphy panel above and a slim pendant lamp beside a small ikebana arrangement

A guest room's private open-air hot-spring bath: a dark stone tub brimming to its rim on a timber deck, a slatted pergola overhead, a bamboo dipper on the edge, enclosed by maples and green undergrowth
A long dark stone hot-spring bath running up to a full-height glass wall, opening onto a deck with reclining loungers and a bank of trees; the water is still enough to mirror the forest
The large public bath: a broad stone pool under a sweeping timber soffit, its far edge open to a landscaped garden of clipped shrubs, moss and a maple turning red
An open-air hot-spring bath filled level with its dark stone coping, a wooden dipper and stool on the rim, screened by maples and a slatted timber fence with the hillside beyond

The library lobby, which houses the tea lounge, bar and dining room: a double-height curved glass wall over the Hakone valley, strings of faceted paper lanterns hanging the full height, pale wood armchairs and cafe tables along the window, a matcha counter with a copper kettle and a wood-burning stove at the back
The drinks cellar: a lit wall of pigeonholes holding sake bottles and stemware beside racked wine, opening onto a dark corridor with a single spotlit ceramic jar

The sashimi course: white fish on a textured glass dish with a yellow flower, sea urchin and sliced fish with shiso blossom in a leaf-shaped bowl, and sweet shrimp in a blue-and-white cup, all set on crushed ice with a maple leaf; a whole wasabi root on a sharkskin grater and dishes of soy and salt alongside
A beef course: two seared cubes of marbled wagyu on a slice of onion with grilled corn, tomato and broccoli, a long grilled sweet potato wedge and a swipe of dark sauce, on a white plate

An appetiser plate: a cut-crystal cup of jellied broth, a small bowl of green paste, pickles in a black dish, a skewered grilled item, a pressed sushi square with crab on a blue-and-white plate, a rolled item and a slice of stuffed courgette, arranged on a round white plate

gora-kadan.caption: Entrance to one of the detached villas: a tiled hip roof over a shingled porch and latticed cedar doors, lit from within, reached by a wet flagstone path winding through the wooded garden between mossy boulders and maples

The guest wing at dusk, its tiers of timber-screened balconies running along a raked white-gravel dry garden set with upright boulders and moss, a bamboo handrail edging the path and a cherry tree in blossom at right, Hakone's hills behind

The long open-sided timber corridor at dusk: a polished plank floor and a colonnade of posts running the length of the building, wicker chairs at the far end, looking out over the treetops to the Hakone mountains

The indoor swimming pool and circular jacuzzi, opening through full-height glass onto a moss-covered boulder cliff and a stand of bamboo and Japanese maple; bamboo-frame loungers with rolled towels along the poolside
A tatami guest room with its full-width doors slid open onto the engawa, framing a wall of red, orange and gold maples in full autumn colour beyond a dark timber railing
A tatami room set with floor cushions and a low table, looking out through the open wall to its own moss-and-stone garden with a steaming open-air stone bath a few steps away

A tatami guest room in the evening: low black dining table on the mats, a window seat and TV console at right, sliding doors open onto a private timber deck with chairs and a lantern, red maples over the garden wall beyond

A contemporary guest room lined floor-to-ceiling in pale timber: a long low sofa, a woven-back armchair and round side table by the window wall, an alcove holding a single ikebana arrangement, sliding glass onto a lawn-and-boulder garden lit at dusk

A guest room's private open-air bath: a broad round stone tub of clear hot-spring water under a slatted timber pent roof, edged with rough boulders and looking straight out over the ryokan's lawn-and-stone garden to the forested Hakone hills

A private open-air bath in a stone-clad oval tub set into a timber deck under a beamed roof, screened by palm and bamboo and looking across a raked gravel garden with a stone lantern and autumn-tinted trees

The public open-air onsen: milky hot-spring water over a pebble and boulder floor, hot water pouring in at the near edge, ceramic lanterns and a red paper wagasa on the stone apron, with the indoor bath visible through open glass doors and maples overhead

The kaiseki dining room in the old villa building: coffered dark-beamed ceiling, alabaster pendant lamps and dark wood tables laid with black lacquer trays and red sake cups, a bay of leaded windows onto orange and red autumn foliage
The sushi counter: an L-shaped bar of unfinished hinoki with pale wood chairs, each place set with a small green dish and chopsticks, a scroll-lit alcove behind and a noren at the kitchen door

A kaiseki course spread: an octagonal wooden tray of hassun bites (pressed sushi, simmered morsels on a leaf-shaped dish, a lidded Kutani pot) with a cut-crystal cup, plus sashimi and tofu with edible flowers, tempura in a woven basket, simmered vegetables in a clay bowl, a red lacquer bowl and a black-and-gold soup bowl
Grilled abalone sliced and returned to its iridescent shell, set on bamboo leaves on a rough ochre ceramic plate, with a small blue-and-white dish of green liver sauce alongside

Marbled wagyu beef cut into cubes with green asparagus, red pepper, squash and turnip on a bamboo leaf in a black-and-white glazed boat-shaped dish, in front of a ceramic tabletop charcoal grill with a wire mesh

gran-class.caption: The GranClass car on the Hokuriku Shinkansen E7: six rows of cream leather armchairs with diamond-quilted backs in a 2+1 layout, wide aisle on deep red carpet, indirect lighting overhead
A GranClass attendant in uniform leaning in to serve a seated passenger from a vacuum flask in the cabin
The GranClass Japanese light meal - a four-compartment lacquer-style box of seasonal dishes served at the seat, shot from above on slate
An E7 series Hokuriku Shinkansen at speed - the ivory, copper-band and deep-blue nose, with the stainless flank of the train stretching back into the cutting

hakone-open-air-museum.caption: Inside the Symphonic Sculpture tower, looking straight up the spiral staircase through the full-height stained glass that wraps the cylinder in fragments of blue, red, amber and green
Autumn in the sculpture garden: a Japanese maple in full orange and scarlet over flowering camellia, with a dark bronze robed figure on a plinth and a gilded sphere sculpture on the lawn beyond

A large bronze reclining figure alone on the open lawn, silhouetted against a forested Hakone ridge under clear sky - the museum's signature sculpture-in-landscape view. The grass and forest are green, so this is a summer photograph
The Picasso Pavilion: the low white building with PICASSO in large black lettering across its facade, and a tall Miro-style painted sculpture standing at the entrance

heki-kintsugi.caption: Kintsugi work by Mio Heki laid out on a pale wood table — a crackle-glass vase with gold seams, a purple-lined tea bowl, a wide Imari plate, a white dish webbed with gold lines and a speckled grey chawan
Lacquer artist Mio Heki in black, brush in hand, working at the villa's window counter with the Higashiyama greenery filling the latticed windows behind her
Heki holding a small black dish and talking a guest through it across the wooden counter, both seated in the window bay of the villa
Hands drawing red urushi lacquer along the mended cracks of an octagonal stoneware dish with a fine brush — the lacquer stage, before the metal powder goes on
Metal powder being brushed onto the wet lacquer seam of a black dish over a lacquer tray, with a cotton ball and a brass coin weight beside it
The villa at dusk: a stone-paved courtyard with bamboo, ferns and floor lanterns leading to the tiled-roof wing, lit shoji glowing along the veranda
The villa's entrance hall: a hammered copper reception desk under a coffered ceiling panel of Nishijin silk woven with peacocks, looking out through a lattice door to the garden

higashi-chaya.caption: The main street of the Higashi Chaya district looking uphill: two-storey wooden teahouses with fine vertical kimusuko lattice screens on both sides, flagstone paving, and the wooded hill closing the view
Inside Kaikaro teahouse: the large banquet ozashiki with bengara-red lacquered walls, a hanging scroll on the end wall, and a broad expanse of tatami where the geiko perform
Kanazawa gold-leaf making: a craftsman's hands lift a single beaten sheet of gold leaf from its interleaving paper with a slender bamboo tool, the stack of hand-treated papers beside it
Kaikaro's gold room: an ochre-gold walled tatami chamber whose matting is woven with gold leaf, set with a lantern, a gilded tea urn and a scatter of small gold cranes

hinanoza.caption: The hotel under snow, with the carved name stone reading "Akan Tsuruga Bessou Hina-no-za" beside the brick approach; guest balconies stack above the covered entrance canopy.
Full facade of the seven-storey building seen from the garden — every guest floor has a screened balcony, since all 25 suites have their own open-air onsen bath.
The entrance court: hand-forged iron lattice screens flanking a carved timber panel inset with a crescent of glass mosaic, over a flagstone floor.

Ten-no-za (天の座) suite in winter — tatami room opening into a wood-floored living area with leather sofas, floor-to-ceiling glass onto the frozen expanse of Lake Akan and the hills beyond. Largest of the five suite types, from 110 sqm.
Umi-no-za (湖の座) suite — tatami dining corner and sunken living area with a massage chair, looking straight down onto Lake Akan with a sightseeing boat passing. From 88 sqm, lake side.
Mori-no-za (森の座) suite — twin low beds on a dark wood floor beside a tatami sitting area, with the vanity and washbasin visible through the open partition. From 61 sqm.
The open-air bath of the 7th-floor public bathhouse "Ishimuro-no-yu Kin-no-Yumi", steaming in cold air behind a slatted timber screen, looking out over the frozen lake and surrounding hills.

A guest-suite open-air bath: a cypress-clad tub with a timber spout, set on the terrace beside the tatami living room with an unobstructed view down the length of Lake Akan. All 25 suites have their own bath.
The 6th-floor public bathhouse "Ishimuro-no-yu Gin-no-Shizuku" — a cut-stone indoor tub under a plank ceiling, with the washing stations along the back wall.
Za-BAR at blue hour — a roughly 10-metre live-edge natural timber counter carved with an Ainu spiral motif, backed by spirit bottles against glass looking onto the snow-covered lakeshore.
A private dining room at the in-house restaurant Ryori-jaya Hina — tatami floor, a heavy dark-lacquer table over a sunken well, and a wall of backlit washi screens with a circular openwork pattern.

The "Sofu-zen" special kaiseki laid out in full: sashimi on crushed ice with botan shrimp and clam, seared wagyu, a claypot of kinki simmered in broth, grilled salmon on a marbled slate, and a dessert plate.
A whole kinki (menme) rockfish simmering in a clay donabe with tofu, daikon and mushrooms, steam rising off the broth.
Hassun course on a ribbed black ceramic plate — grilled scallop, prawn, wagyu cube, a coiled warabi stem and pickled vegetables, with a cut-glass bowl of chilled somen alongside.
The lobby lounge in silhouette: low tables and chairs on a wide plank deck behind slatted timber screens, framing bare winter trees and the snow-covered surface of Lake Akan.

Lake-facing rest corner — a sunken wooden bench pit around a lit stone water basin, with full-height windows onto the frozen lake and snow-laden conifers. The page describes a footbath and free "Akan-ko Hundred-Year Water" spring water served here.

hirata-sword.caption: A bare hand swings the hammer onto a white-hot bar of steel on the anvil, throwing sparks, in the dim forge
The forge building itself: a blue corrugated-metal shed at the roadside in Ome, with wooded hills behind and a hand-lettered wooden sign by the open door
The husband-and-wife smiths, Sukehira and Nodoka Hirata, standing together in the workshop in matching indigo work jackets and black head cloths
The smith bent over the charcoal hearth, drawing a glowing orange billet out of the fire with tongs; rows of forging tools hang on the wall behind
A guest in white cotton work gloves holds a tool alongside the smith, who steadies the glowing steel on the anvil with tongs and raises the hammer
Nodoka Hirata, the furnace (murage) master, explaining the tall clay-lined smelting furnace to a guest inside the workshop
The finished blade the guest takes home: a slim polished small katana signed with the smith's mark in kanji, laid on a cross-cut log

hotel-the-mitsui-kyoto.caption: The Kajiimiya Gate: the 300-year-old tiled and timber gate, its studded doors open onto a pine-and-moss forecourt with a stone pagoda, flanked by white plaster walls.

The hotel at sunset seen across the black-stone water court: three storeys of dark timber louvres and deep eaves wrapping the garden, a big trained pine at right and lit rooms reflected in the shallow pool.
The central Kajitsu garden by day: pond, stone lantern, clipped shrubs and a weeping tree set inside the U of the guest-room wings, with the open-sided lounge visible across the water.
Autumn in the Kajitsu garden: Japanese maples in full red and orange in front of the dark glazed guest-room facade, with a stone lantern and stepping-stone path below.

Nijo Suite living area: slatted-wood feature wall with a carved timber disc, low sofa and live-edge table, and a wide window seat looking over pines to the roofs and stone ramparts of Nijo Castle; the bedroom is visible through the opening at left.
Onsen Suite living area: full-height cedar screen wall, long sofa, live-edge low table and a round dining table beside a glass wall opening onto the suite's own bamboo-screened stone courtyard.
Premier Garden Room with king bed: pale marble headboard wall, walnut desk and a deep timber-framed bay window with a built-in bench looking onto trees and a tiled temple roof.
Deluxe Room with king bed, the entry-level category: marble headboard wall, live-edge bench at the foot of the bed, a walnut tea-and-coffee cabinet, and the glazed bathroom entry beyond.

The Thermal Spring SPA: two guests in swimwear in the warm mineral pool under a column of falling water, surrounded by rough-cut granite boulders, dark stone walls and mirrored ceiling, with loungers along the edge.
The Thermal Spring SPA empty: the mineral bathing pool with two standing granite monoliths, a fine curtain of falling water crossing the room, uplit stone walls and daybeds set on the far bank.

A bookable private onsen: a deep square stone tub filling from a spout, set against a giant boulder and open to a fern-and-ivy planted court behind a dry-stone wall; two guests in robes rest with sparkling wine on the tatami-edged lounge alongside.

Toki, the hotel's Japanese restaurant: the teppan counter with its long mosaic-glass mural, banquette tables beyond, a forest of hanging lantern-tubes under a timber grid ceiling, and full-height glass onto the illuminated garden.

The Shikinoma private dining pavilion: a sukiya-style room with a double-height coffered cedar ceiling, shoji on all sides, an ink-painted panel wall and a single long table, opening onto tatami and the garden.
The Garden Bar at night: two bartenders working behind a long live-edge timber counter with tub chairs, a lit wine wall at left and picture windows onto the floodlit garden.
A course at Toki: a chilled seafood and citrus jelly under a lacy deep-fried tuile, with nasturtium leaves and small white chrysanthemum petals, on a mottled blue-glazed plate.
A seared wagyu course at Toki: a single caramelised beef fillet on a pool of dark reduction, with a nest of fried herbs and a small berry-and-shiso garnish, on a coarse dark stone plate.

hyatt-centric-kanazawa.caption: The hotel tower with its rooftop HYATT CENTRIC sign, seen across the Cross Gate Kanazawa complex; the glass-canopied moving walkway to Kanazawa Station runs along the right edge of the frame.
The porte-cochere at night: illuminated HYATT CENTRIC sign over the entrance, a clipped pine in a planter, and a gold-leaf pine tree artwork on a deep blue ground behind the glass doors.
The lobby — a long communal check-in table with tweed-upholstered chairs on the left, a lacquered red pavilion and a gold-leaf panel wall at the far end, and deep grey sofa groups on the right.
The open-air RoofTerrace Bar on the 14th floor at dusk — woven rattan armchairs and candle-lit tables along a glass balustrade, with the Kanazawa skyline and a pink and purple sunset beyond.
A king guest room: white-linen bed under a large red lacquer relief panel flecked with gold leaf, plaid carpet, a window bench with city view, and a black stone-textured bedside lamp.

A suite living room — deep cobalt-blue feature wall with display shelving and TV, L-shaped sofa with plum and cream cushions facing corner windows over the city, and the bedroom visible through the opening at right.

FIVE - Grill & Lounge in daylight: grey tub chairs at dark square tables on a blue brushstroke rug, a full-height vividly coloured botanical artwork on the left wall, and glazing onto a planted courtyard.
The lounge side of FIVE — pink and navy swivel chairs at round tables, a curved banquette and cane chairs, a dark timber lattice screen, and floor-to-ceiling windows onto the station district.

A grilled steak scored with grill marks on a wooden board with charred vegetables — broccolini, kabocha, sweet potato, mushroom, onion — plus cherry tomatoes, a copper pot of bearnaise, and the raw marbled cut behind.
Six FIVE floor and kitchen staff presenting churrasco-style skewers of shrimp, chicken and beef tableside, carving onto a guest's plate, with the restaurant's botanical artwork behind them.

indigo-ohara.caption: The dye house: three round vats sunk into the concrete floor, their surfaces dark and iridescent, as the dyer in a blue apron and rubber boots reaches into one with a gloved hand; straw bales of indigo stand against the wall
Looking down into a vat as a participant's gloved hands work the cloth under the surface, the coppery-purple liquid crusted with the blue foam dyers call ai-no-hana, the flower of the indigo
The dyer stretching a just-dipped length of gauze up to hang; the cloth is still green and will turn blue as it oxidises in the air, with sacks of fermented indigo behind him
Toru Shimomura, the workshop's owner and dyer, in his pale blue apron holding up an armful of indigo cloth patterned with white shibori sunbursts, dyed hangings and bundled thread behind him

The workshop from outside: a four-panel indigo noren hanging under the deep eaves of the old house, a rack of indigo-dyed smocks and dresses drying along the wall beside it, and a glazed ceramic vat on the step
The finished object the guest takes home: a sheer indigo gauze stole hung in the window, patterned with rows of soft white shibori circles, bare branches visible outside
Finished shibori pieces on the line outdoors — asanoha star lattice, resist-clamped stripes, and rings of white circles — showing the range of patterns the resist techniques produce

itoh-dining-nobu.caption: The restaurant seen from its gravel forecourt: a long low pavilion with a flat metal roof and a full-width glazed front, screened by a rock-and-azalea garden with clipped pines, a navy-and-maroon banner reading ITOH DINING by NOBU on the left.

The main room by day: the teppanyaki counter with black high-backed stools running down the right side toward the griddle and extraction hood, round and rectangular tables at left, and floor-to-ceiling glass opening onto a wooded deck.
A block of wagyu searing on the teppan, crust already formed on top, the chef steadying it with a carving fork and a broad brass spatula.
Plated wagyu: a sliced steak, rare in the middle, on a large speckled grey ceramic plate with a pool of brown sauce, okra, potato crisps and a small savoury galette.
Lobster and a green chilli finishing on the teppan as a domed copper cover is lifted away, steam rolling off the griddle.
Grilled lobster served on a dark green glazed plate with seared scallops and a whole shishito pepper.

kenrokuen.caption: Kasumigaike pond on 9 November: the two-legged Kotoji stone lantern at right, the Uchihashi-tei teahouse on stilts across the water, maples turning scarlet, and the first yukitsuri rope cones already rigged at far left
The Kotoji-toro close up at the water's edge, standing on its two unequal stone legs, with the Uchihashi-tei teahouse blurred behind it across the pond
Yukitsuri: five pines rigged with ropes fanned out from central poles into snow-guard cones, doubled in the still surface of Kasumigaike, photographed 9 November
The winter night illumination at dusk: the yukitsuri cones lit gold above the pond, the Kotoji lantern lit at right, the whole scene doubled in the black water

kikunoi-honten.caption: The Higashiyama street frontage at dusk: two-storey plastered machiya-style building with tiled roof, lanterns lit under the eaves and the carved wooden 菊乃井 signboard at right, approached over a flagstone forecourt framed by bamboo and yellowing autumn foliage

A private tatami dining room: long black-lacquered low table with legless zaisu chairs and cushions, backlit shoji ceiling panel, tokonoma alcove at left, and reed screens opening onto a green garden with a stone lantern

Autumn hassun course: a boat-shaped white dish of assorted seasonal bites - a peeled fruit, a crab-and-vegetable roll, ginkgo- and maple-leaf shaped garnishes and a chestnut-shell cup of salmon roe - set on a woven mat with susuki pampas grass, plus a lacquer bowl of green olives

Chilled squid dish in clear dashi jelly, dusted with red pepper and finished with slivered green vegetable, served in a green Oribe-glazed bowl painted with lotus and geometric motifs, on a bare wood counter
Autumn rice course: sliced matsutake mushrooms folded into soft egg and rice, served in a footed stoneware bowl
Chef-owner Yoshihiro Murata in white chef's jacket embroidered with the Kikunoi crest, photographed at the restaurant entrance

kirishima.caption: Kirishima-jingu head-on from the approach: the vermilion worship hall with its curved copper-green roof and gilded carved gable, flanked by lantern-lit sub-buildings and stone pillars, with dense evergreen forest rising directly behind
Close-up under the shrine eaves: painted and carved shishi lion-dogs, a white dragon and cloud scrollwork in ochre, jade and cobalt against the vermilion beams
Onami-ike, the crater lake in the Kirishima range: turquoise water held in a wooded caldera bowl, seen from the ridge trail with the plank boardwalk descending in the foreground
The volcanic peaks of the Kirishima range from a neighbouring summit - the sharp cone of Takachiho-no-mine with the bare grey Ohachi crater beside it, over rocky scrub in the foreground

kodaiji.caption: The autumn night illumination: floodlit maples in red, orange and gold banked around the Garyu-chi pond and mirrored perfectly in the black water, with the roofed Garyu-ro corridor and a temple roofline lit on the left

The same garden by day in peak autumn: scarlet maples over the Garyu-chi pond, the covered Garyu-ro corridor crossing the water on its posts, the Kaisan-do hall beyond, and fallen red leaves scattered across the moss in the foreground
Kodai-ji's bamboo grove photographed from below, hundreds of green culms rising into backlit leaf canopy

The other half of the night viewing: projection mapping thrown across the raked sand of the Hashintei dry garden and over the temple gate in violet and blue, with red-lit maples behind. Worth knowing this is part of the evening programme, not just plain lighting

kodaiji-jugyuan.caption: A private tatami room glowing at dusk, seen across the garden through red-and-gold autumn maples: shoji panels slid open onto a bamboo-slat veranda, low tables and floor cushions inside, stepping stones leading up from the moss

The large tatami dining room: a long low table with woven zaisu chairs and cushions under hexagonal paper lanterns, carved ranma transoms overhead, and a wall of shoji and glass opening onto the pine-and-rock garden
A single grilled snow-crab leg, shell split to show the white meat, served with half a sudachi on a striped Oribe-style rectangular plate atop a black lacquer tray

Wanmono soup course: lightly seared white fish with a blanched green vegetable and a nest of finely shredded daikon in clear dashi, served in a black lacquer lidded bowl with gold maki-e floral decoration
Two slices of rare, crisply seared beef with a sprig of greens and quartered fresh figs, plated on a dark leaf-shaped ceramic dish on a bare cedar table
A chef in white jacket and cap working at the wooden preparation counter of the villa, framed through the garden's grasses and trees from outside

kokuya.caption: The ryokan's main entrance at night on Shibu Onsen's flagstone lane: pale timber posts, sliding glass doors under a low canopy, an 'ONSEN RYOKAN KOKUYA' sign inside, lit paper panels reading 古久屋, and the lobby with its staircase and rows of guest slippers visible through the glass.

The private entrance to KUON, the ryokan's open-air-bath guest wing: a deep-red noren carrying the Kokuya striped-circle crest under a carved cedar plaque reading 久遠 / SHIBU ONSEN KOKUYA KUON, flanked by two lit paper lanterns.
Two guests in the inn's indigo-striped yukata walking away down the Shibu Onsen stone street on tall wooden geta, photographed low from behind at dusk.

The inn's inner garden at night: a rock-edged pond with three koi, a tall stone lantern, a bamboo shishi-odoshi and a rough stone water basin, set between cedar-boarded walls with a lit bathing room visible through the window behind.

Fukuroku-no-yu, the bath the inn is known for: a row of five separate hinoki tubs under a reed-screened roof, each filled by its own bamboo spout from a different hot spring and labelled with a carved wooden plaque - Jigoku-no-yu, Hana-no-yu, Neruma-no-yu, Ni-no-yu, Zaemon-no-yu - with cypress stools on the boarded floor.

The same row of individual spring-fed hinoki tubs at night, steam rising off the water under warm strip lights, the source name-boards glowing on the cedar wall behind and a potted shrub between the spouts.

A KUON guest room's own open-air bath: a large square hinoki tub filling from a wooden chute on a cypress deck, with a second round copper-banded tub beyond, all enclosed by tall cedar screen walls open to the sky.

A KUON indoor bath: a natural rock-walled pool with hot water running in over the stones, steam filling the room, cedar boarding above and a picture window onto a small courtyard with a stone lantern.

The main room of a KUON suite: a vermilion lacquer table with a honeycomb inlay set over a sunken floor well, low chairs on green cushions bearing the inn's crest, a woven-reed coffered ceiling, a driftwood post and a tokonoma with an ikebana arrangement.
A KUON bedroom: twin beds on a tatami platform with a backlit timber headboard, and above them a small interior window framing a miniature stone garden with a lantern and a red-leafed shrub.

Sagano-no-ma, one of the older open-air-bath rooms: a plain tatami room with a carved rosewood low table and floor chairs, shoji and reed blinds, an arched doorway, and a window onto its private wooden terrace with bonsai and the room's outdoor tub.

Kasumi-no-ma, another open-air-bath room: tatami with a dark lacquered low table and two floor chairs under a bamboo-battened ceiling, and centred in the window the room's own round wooden tub steaming on its private deck.
A private dining alcove: a low table over a sunken leg well with legless chairs on tatami, a shoji screen along one side and a scroll and flower arrangement in the recess behind.

The dining room reserved for KUON guests: a dark wood table and chairs on tatami under a bamboo-lattice ceiling and a cube paper lantern, with a burl-wood plaque reading 久遠 on the wall and the bedroom visible through the opening at right.

The Shinshu-beef shabu-shabu dinner: a plate of heavily marbled beef folded into a rose, a donabe of mushrooms, tofu, greens and udon, a bamboo tray of buckwheat soba, sashimi on an oribe-glazed dish, tempura, grilled fish on a red lacquer plate and an array of small bowls.

A KUON dinner setting: marbled beef with shredded leek on a black checkered plate beside a lit shabu-shabu burner, sashimi of tuna, prawn and white fish on a wooden block, an assorted appetiser plate, chawanmushi, rice, miso soup and pickles.

kurokawa-onsen-town.caption: The Tanoharu river running through the middle of the village at dusk, with timber-and-plaster ryokan stacked up the far bank, their windows and lantern lights reflecting in the water
Two guests in indigo yukata and geta walking down one of the narrow ryokan lanes, past ochre plaster walls, timber lattice and a lit wall lantern
A rock-lined open-air rotenburo half-covered by a moss-grown thatched roof on rough timber posts, boulders standing in the steaming water
Aerial view of the whole village: black-roofed ryokan packed into a narrow wooded valley, cedar plantations and terraced fields around it, with the road curling past on the right

kushiro-shitsugen.caption: The Hosooka Observatory itself: the stone-paved viewing deck, log rail and the carved wooden sign reading Kushiro-shitsugen National Park / Hosooka Observatory, looking out over the marsh running flat to the horizon. The reed beds have already turned straw-gold and the Kushiro River shows as dark threads winding through them, with the ranges of eastern Hokkaido stacked up behind

The marsh in late autumn from the same escarpment: every reed bed burnt tawny-orange, the alder and birch stripped bare, and the Kushiro River curling through the middle of the frame in a wide S-bend of still, pale water. Low raking sun, distant blue hills - this is the closest of the four to what a late-November visit actually looks like

Hoarfrost across the reed bed at sunrise: every stem and seed head rimed white so the whole marsh reads pink-lilac under a low orange sun, with a couple of frozen shrubs standing out and a snow-streaked ridge on the horizon

The Kushiro River in winter, photographed at water level: deep snow lying over the banks and hanging in an overhang above the water, dead standing trees and bleached grass tufts along the edge, and the whole scene doubled in a perfect mirror reflection on the black unfrozen channel under a clear blue sky

kushiro-stay.caption: Nusamai Bridge over the lower Kushiro River - the European-style span with its ornate paired lamp standards and one of the four bronze 'Four Seasons' figures on the parapet
The Kushiro sunset: the sun dropping to the horizon squarely under the middle of Nusamai Bridge, laying a straight column of light down the river, with the bridge and its lamps in silhouette
People lined shoulder to shoulder along the bridge railing at dusk to watch the sun set over the water - the evening ritual behind Kushiro's claim to one of the world's three great sunsets
Kushiro Fisherman's Wharf MOO seen across the river - the pale multi-level waterfront complex with the 'moo' sign, and the domed glass 'EGG' greenhouse building beside it
Downtown Kushiro in deep winter: the river surface covered in 'lotus-leaf ice' with sea smoke drifting off it, snow banked along the riverside street and the town's low blocks behind

kyudo.caption: An archer in white keikogi and muneate chest guard at full draw (kai), black-fletched arrow nocked, the long asymmetric yumi bent across the frame, her form doubled in the dojo's wall mirror

An archer standing in profile in white top and black hakama with bow and arrow lowered, tabi on the polished shooting-hall floor, with the grass range and a row of round mato targets on the far bank behind her
Tight shot at full draw: the white-fletched arrow drawn back past the archer's cheek with a red-bound nock, the string held in a tan leather yugake glove
An instructor in navy work kimono standing behind a Western guest in white gi and black hakama, physically placing the guest's gloved draw hand at the correct height beside his ear
A Western guest at full draw mid-floor in the dojo with a female instructor watching his form from the side; other participants shoot in a line behind him under the wood-panelled ceiling
The dojo interior with the whole wall open to the range: a line of participants in white gi and black hakama kneeling in seiza with eyes closed for the seated meditation that opens the session
An archer in white top, muneate and black hakama smiling as she raises the bow, the yellow-and-purple yugake glove and rattan-wrapped grip of the yumi clearly visible

lake-akan.caption: The Lake Akan boat pier on a freezing morning: frost whitening the decking, steam fog lifting off black water that has not frozen yet, two tour boats moored alongside, and the wooden Akan National Park / Lake Akan sign in the foreground. The far shore is bare-branched with the last brown leaves and low cloud sitting on the ridge

Mount Oakan, the flat-shouldered volcano that stands over the far end of Lake Akan, seen across still water from the reed-fringed shore and framed by a mountain-ash branch in full scarlet autumn leaf. Deep blue sky, the wooded caldera rim running low on both sides

The entrance arch of Akanko Ainu Kotan under deep snow: a carved Blakiston's fish owl with wings spread mounted on the iron arch, two more owls perched at the sides, and the village's timber craft shops and carving workshops running down both sides of the snow-packed street

Marimo underwater: a row of the velvety green algae spheres, roughly grapefruit-sized, resting on the pale sandy lake bed among sunken branches and stones with light filtering down through the water. Lake Akan is the only place in Japan where they grow into balls at this scale, and they are a designated Special Natural Monument

lake-ashi.caption: Hakone Shrine's vermilion Heiwa-no-Torii standing in the shallows of Lake Ashi, photographed from the stone landing beneath it with the far shore and hills behind

The full postcard view: snow-capped Mount Fuji rising beyond the ridge across Lake Ashi, with the red lake torii at the wooded shoreline on the right and a pale evening sky. Shoreline trees are bare and rust-coloured, so this is late autumn or early winter

Autumn colour on the Lake Ashi shore seen from the deck of the sightseeing cruise between Togendai and Hakone-machi: the whole hillside in mixed red, orange and rust against dark cedar, with the vermilion lake torii standing in the water at the shoreline and a wooden jetty beside it

One of the gilded pirate-ship sightseeing boats crossing Lake Ashi under its three masts, framed by overhanging branches from the shore, forested Hakone ridges behind. Foliage is green, so this is a summer photograph

lake-kussharo.caption: Kotan-no-yu, the free open-air hot spring built into the rocks at the very edge of Lake Kussharo: the pool steaming hard in sub-zero air with LADY and MEN bathing signs in the foreground, and forty or fifty whooper swans standing and swimming in the strip of lake water that the geothermal inflow keeps unfrozen. The rest of the lake behind is solid ice, with the snow-covered caldera rim beyond

Dawn at the geothermal lakeshore: sixty or more whooper swans packed into shallow water that is visibly steaming, with a few mallards among them, the mist lit gold by low sun coming through the trees. Every branch and reed on the bank behind is furred white with hoarfrost and there is deep snow to the waterline

The sulphur vents on Mount Io (Iozan / Atosanupuri), a few minutes from the lake: mounds of raw yellow sulphur crystals encrusted around the fumaroles, steam blowing across the frame, and a rope-and-post fence marking how close visitors are allowed to stand. The bare rust-and-grey cone rises behind

Lake Kussharo from high on the caldera rim in late autumn, the classic pass view: Nakajima, the wooded volcanic island, sitting in the middle of open blue water, the lake running away to low hills on every side, and the foreground slopes gone to bleached gold grass with the last rust-coloured leaves in the woods below. No ice yet

leffervescence.caption: The Nishi-Azabu entrance at dusk: a low tiled roof over a ribbed dark-stone facade with the cut-out 'L'Effervescence' lettering, and a lantern-lit stone path leading past planted greenery to the timber front door

The main dining room: white-linen tables with black leather armchairs and a long banquette, under a blackened timber-beam ceiling, with pine arrangements on the back wall and a window onto the garden at left

The restaurant's signature turnip: a whole slow-cooked turnip with its charred stalk left on, set on chervil leaves, a green herb oil line and crumbs of dried brioche, on a plain white plate (file name on source: 'Navet')
A single large ravioli in a dark amber consommé, buried under a heap of thickly shaved white truffle (source file name: 'B-Ravioli')
Roast pigeon: seared breast slices and a leg, with a smear of dark sauce, grilled alliums, morels and grains in an amber jus, in a deep white bowl
Chef Shinobu Namae in a white chef's jacket embroidered 'S. Namae', photographed by a window inside the restaurant

lexus-nx-japan.caption: A dark grey NX 350h hybrid seen from the rear three-quarter, driving a two-lane road that curves through green coastal hills with the sea visible to the right

The front cabin from the passenger side: ivory perforated leather seats and door trim against a dark grey dashboard, the centre touchscreen angled toward the driver and a right-hand-drive steering wheel

The driver's cockpit: right-hand-drive steering wheel, digital instrument binnacle and the large centre touchscreen running Apple CarPlay with the Japanese-language interface, above the console gear selector and cup holders

meiji-jingu.caption: The great cypress torii (Otorii) on the main approach, framing the wide gravel sando as it disappears into the shrine forest; visitors walking through give the scale
The main worship hall (gehaiden) seen across the open gravel courtyard, with its sweeping copper roof and camphor trees to either side

The forest approach: the paved path curving under the dense canopy of the planted evergreen woodland that surrounds the shrine. Foliage is green here, so this is a warm-season photograph rather than late November
The wall of consecrated sake barrels (kazaridaru) stacked beside the approach, each painted with a brewery's name, with visitors passing in front

mutoh-kintsugi.caption: Four finished kintsugi pieces on a dark table — a white bowl with a green shard set back in, a blue-and-white rice bowl, a grey tea bowl and a cut-glass bottle, all with branching gold seams
The gold work itself: a fine brush drawing a gold line along the mended crack of a grey-glazed bowl held in the other hand
A participant at the studio workbench, brush in hand, turning the bowl to reach the seam; jars of brushes, coloured glass palettes and a sprig of maple sit on the bench beside her
The starting point: two hands holding a broken speckled stoneware bowl with its detached shard lifted away, on a kraft-paper work mat
The kit laid out: a tube of kintsugi lacquer (金継ぎ用漆), a sachet labelled pure gold powder (純金粉), turpentine, a glass mixing plate, sandpaper, cotton wadding, a bamboo spatula and two brushes
Inside Mutoh's Nihonbashi shop where the workshop is held: lit shoji panels, wall shelving of lacquerware and glass, and display tables of red-and-black lacquer trays and bowls
The shopfront at dusk on a Nihonbashi street: black timber facade, glowing interior and a white noren whose right panel reads 器 日本橋 武藤 本店 (Utsuwa Nihonbashi Mutoh Main Store)

okas-sankara.caption: Okas's dining room on the second floor of the main building: a long counter facing the open kitchen under a pitched timber roof, with glass on both sides looking into the forest and out toward the sea
One of Okas's curved upholstered booths laid for two at dusk, with the window looking over palms to the darkening ocean
A slice of pate en croute - layered meat and foie gras in a burnished pastry case - served with a pink granita, edible flowers and a citrus gel
Main course: a glazed fillet in a dark reduction with baby carrots, green pea puree quenelles and shaved vegetables on a fluted white plate
An amuse served in a footed glass - caviar and herbs over a pale mousse on a tomato base, finished with a lace tuile and a blue flower
A chef in whites finishing a plate at the pass, spooning sauce from a copper pan over a serving of beef with vegetables

omotesando-ginkgo.caption: The Jingu Gaien ginkgo avenue at full autumn colour: four rows of conically pruned ginkgo in solid gold running down Aoyama-dori toward the domed Meiji Memorial Picture Gallery, under a clear blue sky
Looking up into the tops of the Gaien ginkgo in peak yellow against blue sky and cloud, the fan-shaped leaves fully turned

The reality of late November: dense crowds filling the ginkgo avenue during the Jingu Gaien Ginkgo Festival, food stalls at the far end and the Picture Gallery dome in the distance, leaves half green and half gold

Omotesando boulevard at dusk seen from the pedestrian bridge, the zelkova (keyaki) canopy arching over both sides of the street above the flagship stores and traffic. Foliage is green, so this is a warm-season photograph, not late November

palace-hotel-tokyo.caption: The hotel's white curved facade rising behind the Imperial Palace moat, with the Tatsumi watchtower and its stone rampart in the foreground and red autumn maples at right
The hotel seen across the Imperial Palace moat, two swans on the water and the moat's stone embankment and tree line running the length of the frame
Autumn view from the hotel over the Imperial Palace outer gardens, maples in full red and gold colour, with the Marunouchi and Toranomon skyline and Tokyo Tower behind

The main lobby: a gold-leaf screen wall depicting pines and irises on the left, a round table with a large floral arrangement, and floor-to-ceiling glass looking out to a red maple against the moat's stone wall
Deluxe Room with Balcony: king bed, wood-panelled headboard wall, and a full-width sliding glass door onto a private balcony with chairs, overlooking the palace greenery
Grand Deluxe Room with Balcony seen from the bedside: armchairs and a tea service on a round table, with the balcony and the wooded Imperial Palace grounds through the glass
Chiyoda Suite bedroom at night: low platform bed in blond wood, slatted timber screen behind the headboard, and lit high-rise towers through the window
Chiyoda Suite bathroom: green-marble deep soaking tub filling from a wall spout beside a window, glass walk-in rain shower, and a dark stone double vanity with amenities
Grand Deluxe Room bathroom at night: limestone vanity with mirrored wall, separate glass shower, and a soaking tub set against a window over the lit city
The hotel's indoor swimming pool at dusk with a circular jacuzzi in the foreground, red loungers, and floor-to-ceiling windows over the palace grounds and Tokyo skyline
Wadakura, the hotel's Japanese restaurant: wood tables with lacquer trays and a black rough-hewn stone wall, glass on the left looking over the moat and palace gardens
Esterre, the Alain Ducasse restaurant: round tables in cream linen with candle lamps, sculpted upholstered chairs, framed botanical studies on the wall and a lit fireplace at the back
The Royal Bar: plum velvet wingback armchairs around a figured-marble table, backed by lit glass shelves of whisky, cognac and cut-crystal glassware
In-room dining breakfast served on a guest-room balcony: omelette with ham and salad, croissant and bread basket, juice and sparkling water, on a wooden table above the palace moat and gardens

Crab course from a Wadakura kaiseki menu: steamed snow-crab legs and shoulder meat with picked crab and crab miso served in the shell, carved cucumber and radish garnish and sudachi, on a rustic glazed plate
Esterre plate: poached lobster tail crowned with caviar, green asparagus and a herb foam in an orange lobster bisque, in a wide off-white bowl

philosophers-path.caption: Honen-in's thatched sanmon gate in autumn: the low pyramidal roof carpeted in deep green moss, framed by maples in orange and scarlet, with more gold foliage visible through the open gateway and worn mossy stone steps climbing to it. Photographed 10 December, at the tail of the maple season

The approach to Honen-in: a flagstone path crossing a small wooden bridge over a mossy stream, thick moss carpeting the ground on both sides, maples overhead just turning from green to orange, and the thatched gate visible at the top of the steps beyond

The Philosopher's Path itself: the narrow stone-walled canal running dead straight beside the paved walkway, cherry trees arching over both, a man sitting on the parapet sketching. Trees are in full green leaf, so this is a summer photograph rather than late November

Honen-in's gate seen from inside the grounds: the thatched sanmon at the head of a broad flight of mossy stone steps, with the temple's two flat raked white-sand beds (byakusadan) flanking the flagstone path in the foreground. Foliage is green, so this is a spring photograph

ritz-carlton-fukuoka.caption: The hotel tower at dusk, its cantilevered glass upper block lettered THE RITZ-CARLTON, rising above the low-rise Tenjin district with the mountains behind Fukuoka on the horizon
The street entrance at night: a bronze-toned portal of perforated metal screens studded with small pendant lights, framing a lit corridor that leads inward to a large flower arrangement
Sunset from the hotel's open-air rooftop terrace, looking west over the Fukuoka skyline with Fukuoka Tower, the domed stadium and Hakata Bay under an orange sky
Ohori Park, the large lake park a short walk from the hotel, with its vermilion arched bridge and green-roofed floating pavilion mirrored in still water against the city skyline and mountains
Guest room with a king bed, pale wood joinery and grey fabric wall panels, floor-to-ceiling windows looking over Hakata Port to the bay, a moored cruise ship and the red-and-white port tower
Guest room with king bed, window bench, round table and armchair set into the corner window, looking out over the Fukuoka cityscape to the mountain range beyond
Suite living and dining area: an eight-seat dining table under an alabaster-petal chandelier with a sumi-e ink work on the wall, low sofa along the window, and city-and-mountain views on two sides
Suite bathroom with a twin-basin vanity carved from heavily veined marble and tall mirrors, set directly against a floor-to-ceiling window over Ohori Park, the city and distant mountains

The indoor pool: a long turquoise-tiled pool under a slatted wood ceiling and cylindrical pendant lamps, with marble piers on one side and a wall of glass framing the Fukuoka skyline and Hakata Bay; a guest reclines on a daybed at the far end
A spa treatment room set for two, with side-by-side tables, a dark marble wet counter with a stone basin, woven-front cabinetry and a therapist carrying folded towels

The lobby lounge on the sky-lobby level: double-height windows hung with sheer mesh screens, a lit washi-panel wall, herringbone floors, and low seating grouped around a large iris arrangement, with the city and bay visible outside

The sushi counter at the hotel's Japanese restaurant: a long blond hinoki counter set with glass rests and chopsticks, spindle-back chairs, a folded metallic ceiling above and windows onto the city and Hakata Bay

The teppanyaki counter at night: a U-shaped live-edge timber counter wrapping a steel griddle under a brass extraction canopy, leather armchairs, a rough stone artwork behind and the lit city skyline through the window
A thick cut of marbled wagyu searing on the teppanyaki griddle, crusted brown on top and still rare through the middle

A plated raw-fish course at the hotel's Western restaurant: sliced white fish with caviar, micro herbs, shaved cucumber and red onion over a saffron-coloured sauce on a matte ceramic plate, with a glass of white wine alongside
A lacquer bowl of white-miso soup with sea bream, daikon, carrot, greens and a dot of mustard, shot from above on a lacquered table with the restaurant's printed chopstick sleeve in front

rurikoin.caption: The signature view from the second-floor Ruri-no-ma: a hillside of scarlet, orange and gold maples filling the open window bays, mirrored in the polished black lacquer writing table below
Wider view of the same second-floor room, showing the full length of the lacquered table and the tatami floor also picking up the reflection of the autumn maples outside
The ground-floor tatami room opening onto the Ruri-no-niwa moss garden: a flat carpet of bright green moss under maples turning red, framed by the open shoji bays
The temple approach: stone steps and the wooden entrance gate in its earthen wall, under maples in mixed red, orange and yellow

sakurajima.caption: Sakurajima at blue hour, seen from above Kagoshima across the bay: a white gas plume drifting off the summit, the lit downtown high-rises and the ferry terminal in the foreground
A dark ash column punching straight out of the summit crater against blue sky, with the bare grey ash-covered upper slopes below
The volcano from the Arimura Lava Observatory on its south side - the eroded cone close up, with young pines growing out of the black lava field in front of the observatory's log railing

The long free foot bath at Yogan Nagisa Park on Sakurajima's waterfront: a stone channel of hot spring water with wooden slat seats along it, the bay and the Kagoshima hillside opposite behind the railing. Photographed 9 November

sankara-yakushima.caption: Aerial view of the resort at first light: a scatter of low villa roofs and the lit pool terrace set into dense forest on the hillside above the Pacific
The main building at dusk, warm-lit behind its glass wall, with the infinity pool in the foreground and Yakushima's ridge line rising behind
Villa roofs among palms and subtropical planting, with the open ocean horizon beyond
The infinity pool on a clear day - timber jetty over a black reflecting basin, canvas parasols and loungers, and the Pacific filling the horizon
Yakushima's interior: a mist-filled ravine of cedar and broadleaf forest above a boulder-strewn stream, the landscape the hotel sits in
Villa Suite living room under an exposed timber ceiling, glass wall sliding open onto a private deck with loungers and an ocean view
Villa Suite bedroom with twin beds in green and white linen, ceiling fan and cedar ceiling; the villa's private sauna cabin is visible through the terrace door
Manasa Villa bedroom - twin beds against a timber headboard wall, corner windows and a balcony door opening onto forest
Junior Suite: sitting area in the foreground opening through a wide portal to the bed and a balcony framing the sea
Open-air soaking tub on a Villa Suite deck - a round dark stone bath with a floor-standing spout, screened by bamboo balustrade and tropical planting, looking out to the ocean
Suite bathroom: a deep sunken stone soaking tub and a separate walk-in rain shower, with a bamboo lattice screen filtering green light from the forest outside
Suite bathroom with a freestanding oval tub set against a floor-to-ceiling glass wall that opens straight onto the trees
okas, the hotel's French restaurant - a single long communal table laid with place settings, lit low, against a full-height glass wall onto the forest
ayana, the second restaurant: a long narrow room of exposed brick and dark timber with white-clothed tables and an open kitchen at the far end
A composed course at okas - marinated fish under a thin white sheet, scattered with edible flowers, pickled beetroot and oil dots on a wide white plate
Seafood paella in a black iron pan - squid, prawns, octopus and snow peas over saffron rice, from the ayana menu

sanzen-in-ohara.caption: The Ojo Gokuraku-in (Amida hall) seen head-on from the gravel path, standing on its moss carpet in the Yusei-en garden and ringed by maples in full orange and red
One of the warabe-jizo: a small round-faced stone child-Buddha lying on its side, half swallowed by the deep green moss of the garden floor
The Shuheki-en garden seen from inside the Kyaku-den across a red felt bench and tatami: clipped shrubs, a stone lantern and pond, with maples turning red behind (official temple photograph)
The stone-stepped approach lane up to the temple in late November, the inscribed pillar reading Sanzen-in Monzeki, under maples in crimson and gold

shinkansen-green-car.caption: The N700S Green Car cabin looking down the aisle: two seats either side of a wide centre aisle, deep burgundy diamond-weave upholstery with white head covers and tan leather-topped armrests, a continuous warm LED cove running the length of the curved ceiling, and the destination display lit at the far vestibule. The overhead row markers read 17 A/B on one side and 17 C/D on the other, which is the 2+2 Green Car layout

Close-up of the Green Car seat controls on the aisle armrest: reading-light and recline buttons plus a lit green leg-rest indicator on a brushed metal plate, a two-pin mains socket moulded into the armrest shell beside them, and the fold-out armrest table above. The diamond-lattice moquette of the seat cushion fills the frame - this is woven fabric, not leather

A sixteen-car N700S on the Tokaido main line at Higashi-Tagonoura with Mount Fuji filling the sky behind it, snow still on the cone. The blunt, flat-fronted N700S nose and the N700 Supreme script on the car side are both clearly readable, and the train is crossing a low viaduct over farmland

N700S set J2 in three-quarter view from above, running beside open water on the Tokaido line: the full white-and-blue flank, the sculpted dual-supreme-wing nose, and the pantograph and catenary above. The clearest single look at the current Tokaido train

shiratani-unsuikyo.caption: The Mossy Forest (Kokemusu-no-mori) — the section said to have inspired Princess Mononoke: every boulder, root and fallen trunk under a green fur of moss, with two hikers sitting on a log at right for scale

Nidai-Osugi, a hollow-trunked yakusugi cedar on the Shiratani trail — the trailside marker gives it as 32 m tall, 4.4 m girth, at 730 m elevation — with a family of three walking past below it and a moss-covered boulder in the foreground

Taiko-iwa, the granite slab at the far end of the Shiratani course at about 1,050 m, with two hikers sitting on the edge looking across the forested interior ridges of Yakushima and the river gorge below
A Yakushika deer standing in the clear green water of the ravine stream, moss-covered banks and low overhanging branches on both sides
Close-up of the moss itself — a dense mat of star-shaped haircap moss, wet, with a single broadleaf seedling pushing up through it

shiroyama-kagoshima.caption: Aerial view of the whole hotel: long red-brick wings wrapped around the crown of the Shiroyama hill, with the outdoor pool terrace, garden lawns and the porte-cochere below, and Kagoshima's suburbs and green hills stretching away behind
The hotel from below, its red-brick facade running along the top of the densely wooded Shiroyama bluff with the crest badge on the central tower, seen against a clear sky

The hotel at dusk with its guest-room windows lit orange, the long outdoor pool and brick terrace in the foreground, a lantern-lined path down the hillside, and the lights of central Kagoshima on the plain below
The hotel's brick terrace with its circular fountain, café tables and yellow parasols beside a glass-walled restaurant, looking out across Kinko Bay to the Sakurajima volcano

The open-air hot-spring bath Satsuma-no-yu: a long infinity-edge pool of clear water under a slatted cedar canopy, a bather resting on the rim, azaleas along the parapet, and the whole panorama of Kagoshima city, Kinko Bay and Sakurajima beyond
The same open-air bath at dawn: a bather at the infinity edge with steam on the water, the sun rising directly behind Sakurajima's smoking cone and the city lights still on below
Sunrise from inside the open-air bath, shot into the light: the bath edge and canopy in silhouette, a gold sun-track across the still water, and Sakurajima in violet haze across the bay

A classically furnished suite living and dining room with a long mahogany table, Empire-style armchairs, a green patterned carpet and writing desk, its corner windows looking straight out at Sakurajima and down over the city and bay

A twin guest room on the Sakurajima-view floor: two beds with carved wooden headboards and red bench ends, a wing chair and ottoman, a writing desk set into the window, and Sakurajima and the bay filling the corner glazing

A Japanese-modern room at night: twin beds on a raised tatami platform behind a light-timber dining table with slatted-back armchairs, indirect cove lighting, a hanging lantern, and floor-to-ceiling glass onto the garden

The breakfast buffet: a long chafing-dish line in the foreground loaded with sausages, ham, fried fish, salads, a whole platter of sashimi and a soup cauldron, with rows of white-clothed tables behind and a wall of windows framing Sakurajima

The teppanyaki restaurant Kusunoki: a long polished mahogany counter with two steel griddles under a suspended copper hood, striped armchairs along it, and glass walls onto a lit garden where a maple has turned red

A plated seafood starter with caviar, herbs and coloured sauces on a square white plate, laid on a white-linen table with two glasses of red wine, a votive candle and a small posy, against the bokeh of Kagoshima's night lights through the restaurant window
A breakfast rice bowl in black lacquer, topped with thick shavings of dried bonito, sliced spring onion and a raw egg yolk, with soy sauce being poured over from a lacquer pourer

shoraku-raku.caption: The tea room entrance at the kiln: a plaster-and-timber building behind a mossy boulder wall, short noren over the door, framed by pine and a maple turning orange
The potter seated in the workshop in a dark work jacket, cradling a raw clay bowl on his knee and shaping it with a hand tool; racks of pots stand behind him
Close-up of hands carving the outside of a leather-hard chawan with a blade on a small iron turntable, curls of clay shavings piled around it
The potter leaning in to guide a participant's cut, both holding red-handled trimming blades over her half-carved tea bowl in the workshop room
The finished object: a black raku tea bowl (kuro-raku chawan) with an irregular lip and pitted glossy glaze, on a plain wood table
The tea room where the ceremony is held: tatami with a sunken ro hearth and iron kettle, hanging scroll and flower in the tokonoma, host kneeling by the fusuma

snow-monkeys.caption: About a dozen macaques soaking together in the park's hot-spring pool with no snow anywhere — from the park's own autumn gallery, and the realistic version of the famous shot for a late-November visit
The postcard image: two macaques grooming chest-deep in the steaming pool during falling snow, snowflakes settled on their fur — this is deep winter (roughly January-February), not late November
An adult macaque sitting on the wet grey rock slabs of the gorge with the valley behind it in full orange-and-yellow autumn colour — the park's own autumn gallery
An adult macaque perched on fallen branches in the leaf-littered hillside forest, foliage mostly down and yellowed — late-autumn conditions in the woods around the park
The yumichi — the roughly 1.6 km forest approach trail to the park — carpeted in fallen yellow leaves, with a wooden rail on the ravine side and cedars above

The hot-spring pool seen wide with no snow on the ground: visitors in coats standing and photographing from the path a couple of metres away while monkeys sit on the pool rim and in the water, steam rising, the river and rock wall of the gorge behind

sowaka.caption: The hotel's street frontage on Shimogawara-dori in Higashiyama at dusk: the two-storey wooden main house on the left, the timber-latticed annex on the right, and the dark SOWAKA noren over the stone entry lane between them.
Inner court of the modern annex, walled in charred black cedar, with a raked gravel bed, slender young maples, stepping stones and a hanging iron lantern seen from a covered wooden deck.

The main house's central courtyard garden in daylight, ringed on three sides by the 1920s wooden building with its second-floor balcony; moss, stepping stones, a leaning pine and maples just turning red and yellow.

The same courtyard garden lit at dusk, with a bamboo water spout in the foreground and a guest room glowing behind the trees; the wrapping timber-and-plaster galleries of the main house rise on all sides.
The courtyard garden framed from inside a guest room: moss, stepping stones, a red-leafed shrub and old trunks, with the round moon-window wall of the tea room on the right.
The rooftop terrace, set with a chilled bottle and two glasses, looking out over Higashiyama tiled roofs to the Kyoto hills beyond.

The Garden View Suite (room 108) in the wooden main house: a low bed on tatami, sofa and daybed, exposed timber beams and a slatted wood ceiling, with shoji and a glazed veranda opening onto the treetops.
Main-house room 106 (Higashiyama View): twin beds set low on tatami under a coffered cedar ceiling, a live-edge low table, rattan chairs and full-width shoji screens.
A ground-floor main-house guest room seen from the courtyard at dusk with its sliding screens open: bed, seating alcove and a raised wooden engawa running along the garden edge.

Annex room 205 (Courtyard View with Open-Air Bath): earth-plaster walls, a pair of leather lounge chairs and a round table at a full-height window looking onto a planted terrace over an old tiled roof; an antique red lacquer apothecary chest at right.
Bathroom of the Casita room (111): twin dark stone basins on a walnut counter, dark tiled walls, and a hinoki soaking tub beside a glass wall onto a small bamboo courtyard with a second outdoor tub.
Annex room 207: a free-standing square hinoki cypress tub set in the middle of a dark-tiled bathroom, facing a full-height glass wall onto a private planted court enclosed by charred cedar boards.

The hotel's restaurant, Gion Loka: a long stone counter with leather chairs on one side, tables laid with wine glasses on the other, dark plaster walls, and a glazed wall onto a green inner courtyard.
Gion Loka's table seating along the courtyard glazing, with round and rectangular tables set with placemats and glassware, dark concrete floor and ceiling, and maples and ferns lit outside.
A sashimi course on a grey ceramic plate: seared scallop, tuna, sea bream, squid and a whole prawn with edible flowers, watermelon radish, myoga, wasabi and two dipping sauces.
