A hassun course served on a glass-topped cedar tray: bamboo shoots and greens under a domed lid, grilled fish in broth with myoga, beef rolls with mustard and flowering herbs, croquettes and a lacquered mould.

teamlab.caption: teamLab Borderless, Azabudai Hills: a room with no screen edges - projected chrysanthemums and peonies in hot pink, red and yellow cover the floor, the walls and a low central mound, while a river of fine blue light-threads pours down the far wall and streams out across the floor. Four visitors are inside the projection; a small child sits on the floor in the middle of it, which shows how the imagery wraps around people rather than facing them

Universe of Water Particles on a Rock where People Gather: the same room rendered entirely in blue and white. Simulated water falls in vertical threads down every wall, breaks over a solid rock mound in the centre of the floor, and spreads outward in wide spiralling eddies across the ground. Visitors stand on and around the rock, and the flow visibly deflects around each of them

Infinite Crystal World: a mirror-floored, mirror-walled room hung with dense curtains of point LEDs on hanging strands, lit here in warm gold above and deep blue below. One visitor stands alone in the middle, silhouetted, with a clean reflection beneath - the mirrors repeat the light field outward so the room reads as endless

teamLab Planets, Toyosu - Drawing on the Water Surface Created by the Dance of Koi and People: two visitors stand barefoot in knee-deep water in a darkened hall while projected koi swim around their legs, each fish trailing a broad ribbon of magenta, yellow and cyan light that curls into a vortex where the water is disturbed. You walk into this one; the water is real and you are wet to the knee

Floating Flower Garden at teamLab Planets: several thousand living orchids suspended on hanging roots, filling the room floor to ceiling, above a mirrored floor that doubles them. Two visitors in white stand inside the mass of flowers - the blooms lift as you approach and close again behind you, so you are enclosed on all sides

tofukuji.caption: The Tsutenkyo covered bridge-corridor spanning the Sengyokukan ravine, seen across a sea of crimson and orange maples at peak autumn colour
The maple valley below Tsutenkyo in full autumn colour, with visitors lined along the bridge railing in the middle distance
The north garden of the Hojo: squares of moss set into white gravel in a checkerboard that dissolves toward the far corner, laid out by Mirei Shigemori in 1939

The Hojo south garden from the veranda: four groups of upright stones set in raked gravel with moss mounds to the right, framed by the karamon gate and the temple roofs behind (official temple photograph)

tsurui-cranes.caption: Red-crowned cranes on a bare, straw-coloured field with no snow at all, one bird head-back in full call — the early-season look, before eastern Hokkaido whitens over
The feeding ground at the Tsurui-Ito Tancho Sanctuary: roughly eighty cranes spread across the open field under a thin snow cover, with brown reeds and the larch and birch woodland behind
A pair of red-crowned cranes in flight low over the field, wings fully extended and legs dropping to land, dark winter woodland behind
The courtship dance: one crane leaping with wings thrown wide while its partner rises beneath it, kicked-up snow backlit by low sun through bare larches
The landscape the cranes roost in: a flock standing overnight in the shallow, unfrozen river with every branch on the banks coated in hoarfrost — this is deep midwinter, not late November

uji-matcha-kane7.caption: Kane7's tea rows growing under black shade netting — the covered cultivation (ooishita) used to grow tencha, the leaf that is later stone-milled into matcha
Proprietor Tomoharu Hatakeyama talking a guest through the tea across the counter; a bamboo whisk and chashaku scoop and a stone mill sit between them, tea bowls on the shelves behind
A guest hand-turning the granite tea mill (ishi-usu), tencha leaf in the hopper and freshly ground matcha powder spilling out around the rim onto the collecting dish
Matcha being measured with a bamboo chashaku into a glazed tea bowl on tatami, natsume caddy and bamboo chasen whisk alongside — the tea-ceremony portion of the experience
The traditional tatami tea room used for the ceremony: tokonoma alcove with a hanging calligraphy scroll and single flower, and a sunken ro hearth cut into the mats
The modern tasting counter at KANE7 Matcha Lab — concrete-and-oak island with four stools, iron kettle on the hob, and lit shelves of tea bowls and kyusu along the back wall
Leaf-shaped matcha confections on gilded dishes in a lacquer-and-paulownia box, with a mound of matcha powder in a gold vessel — the sweets course made by Shinsuke Kimura of Treee's Kyoto

yakushima-coast.caption: Oko-no-taki: a wide white cascade sliding down a bare granite slab on a steep forested mountainside, low cloud hanging over the ridge behind and dense broadleaf canopy on all sides
Nagata Inakahama: a long curve of pale gold sand with clear turquoise shallows breaking onto it and a dark green forested headland at the far end

The west-coast road on the Western Forest Road side of the island, running along a steep green hillside with a low blue guardrail, the deep-blue sea and a chain of forested headlands stretching away to the north
Sunrise from high on Yakushima: the sun coming up over an unbroken sea of cloud with the island's forested ridges falling away in layers below, wind-shaped yakusugi in the foreground

yanaka-tokyo.caption: The entrance gate to Yanaka Ginza, its wooden arch carrying the shopping street's name in kanji, with the narrow lane of shops running away downhill behind it and cat-themed shop banners on the right
Inside Yanaka Ginza: grilled-squid and snack stalls under cloth awnings, two women in yukata eating at a low table on the street, bicycles and shoppers filling the pedestrian lane
A quiet Yanaka back lane in low afternoon sun: an inscribed temple boundary stone, wooden fences and low houses, overhead power lines and almost no traffic

One of Yanaka's famous stray cats, a black cat sitting on a granite grave in Yanaka Cemetery among flower offerings. The cherry tree overhead is in full bloom, so this is a spring photograph, not late November

yufuin.caption: Lake Kinrinko in autumn: steam lifting off the warm water into cold morning air, a maple in full scarlet on the near bank, yellow and orange trees along the far shore and the mountains behind
Yunotsubo Kaido, the town's main shopping street, lined with white-plaster and dark-timber shopfronts, with the twin summits of Mt Yufu rising straight up at the end of the road
The twin-peaked cone of Mt Yufu above open grassland, with two cars on the highway curving across the foreground
Dawn on Lake Kinrinko, mist rolling off the surface in front of the tall cedars on the far bank, with a wooded ridge to the left

zeniya-kanazawa.caption: The restaurant's street entrance at night: a lit stone-and-timber doorway off Katamachi with an illuminated white sign reading 日本料理 銭屋 (Japanese Cuisine Zeniya), opening onto a flagstone approach.
The ground-floor counter room: a long unfinished hinoki counter with about seven slip-covered chairs, hanging paper lanterns, and the open finishing kitchen with its grill and tiled back wall behind.

An autumn hassun course seen from above: turquoise leaf-shaped dishes of grilled eel, shrimp, tamagoyaki, sweet potato, okra and yamamomo set on crushed ice, with cut-crystal cups of dressed greens, maple leaves and orange hozuki lanterns.
Sashimi on a hammered silver-grey plate: a grilled langoustine tail, a slice of white fish, cubes of fatty tuna, shredded citrus, wasabi, purple shiso flowers and micro-shiso.
Steamed abalone served in its own shell on a blue-and-white Imari plate with seaweed and red peppercorns, the dish set outdoors on a moss bed among ferns.
Portrait of the chef in a white jacket and folded paper cap, the jacket embroidered with the Zeniya crest and the name 髙木 (Takagi).

zenkoji.caption: The Hondo, Zenko-ji's enormous all-wood main hall, from the side: a deep shingled roof over a T-shaped plan, with clipped pines and stone lanterns in front (official temple photograph)

The Niomon gate seen head-on from the bottom of its stone steps, the plaque reading Jogakusan under a swooping copper-green roof, with the Nio guardians in their side bays and offerings of straw sandals hung on the grilles
The Nakamise approach street: shops and banner poles on both sides of the paved way, visitors walking up toward the Sanmon gate, with the wooded hills behind the temple
A robed procession under tall red ceremonial parasols drawn up in front of the Hondo, either side of the eko-bashira pillar - it gives a sense of the hall's scale
